title: Mogshade Course Case Seara
body_html:
Mogshade's 'Seara' Course Case is handmade with rescued high-quality wool fabrics woven at factories in the mountain region of Serra da Estrela. The inside, crafted with cotton lining, is equipped with a pocket to hold ball markers and with loops to keep a few tees close. The rest is left open for a rangefinder, valuables, or whatever finds its way into the bag. The case comes with a metal carabiner.

Features

Diameter of approx. 14-15cm.
Fits all typically-sized rangefinders.
Internal velcro pocket and tee loops.
Metal carabiner and woven webbing strap at rear.

Fabric detail

Outer Shell: 100% wool
Lining: 100% deadstock polyester
Brand Labels: 100% recycled polyester
Thread: 100% polyester
Metal Carabiner
Climbing cord zipper puller

Cleaning

If your case gets excessively wet, promptly hang or lay it flat to dry. Additionally, consider placing crumpled paper balls, like newspaper, inside to absorb excess moisture.

Before attempting to clean and remove spots or stains, always test cleaning methods in an inconspicuous area to ensure the mild detergent or the mild brushing will not alter the colour or the texture of the fabric. Try using warm water (max 30ºC).

We advise against ironing, dry cleaning, and the use of washing machines and tumble dryers.

title: Depeche Golf Issue 5 - Home
body_html:
The issue looks into places and ideas related to the concepts behind the word HOME.

We headed up to St Andrews where the historic home of golf is constantly changing; we made the road our home for a wild summer of golf in Ireland and visited the Engadine Golf Club in St Moritz, a mountain town widely seen as the Swiss home of golf. We portrayed the guys from our home course down the road and went on a quest for the vanishing greens of Singapore. We were guests at the world’s oldest building used as a clubhouse and visited an artist in New Zealand who built an unplayable golf course through his hometown Christchurch. We dove into the philosophy of home and considered the nature of the flag. We went looking for Missing Links in the far-east, had a lesson with the Old Pro and learnt there is finally a doctor on the course, while our Photographer in Residence brought us views of other people’s homes and courses.

Brim full of stories, art and fabulous photography, number five will shift your perspective. Because… This game deserves more.

title: 'Eighteen' Mono
body_html:
Golf does not only live on the course. It lives in clubhouses, homes, studios, pro shops, corners of memory, and the objects we choose to keep around us.

With Loomed Rounds, Mogshade and Soft Hands Club bring the game into those spaces in the form of wool posters.

Handmade-to-order in Serra da Estrela, Portugal, each piece is produced using 100% burel wool and finished with oak wood.

The artworks draw from the golden age of modernism in Portugal and from the visual language of Maria Keil, whose bold use of colour, geometry, and composition helped shape Portuguese graphic design and tilework. The shapes echo the Lisbon Metro stations she designed, reinterpreted here through the language of golf. Fairways, flags, and natural elements become woven surfaces.

‘Eighteen’ in Mono is the last chapter on the scorecard. Made literal but subtle.

Each design will be produced in a limited number of three pieces only, in a 70 × 50 cm format. Handmade to order. Please allow 6-8 weeks for delivery.

title: Dimple & Divot x Gumtree Golf & Nature Club – Species Brush Shagbark Hickory
body_html:
These Gumtree Golf & Nature x Dimple & Divot premium golf brushes are made in the US and carved from three different species of American trees. All brushes feature a nickel trigger snap and tonal paracord to match the natural wood tones. 

The Shagbark Hickory (Carya ovata) is a tree that feels both rugged and refined. The kind you notice not for its perfection, but for its personality. Its tall, straight trunk is wrapped in strips of curling bark that peel away like old parchment, revealing a silvery smoothness beneath. Found across the eastern woodlands, it’s a tree of deep roots and slow reward,  its nuts feeding wildlife and its wood prized for warmth, smoke, and strength.

title: Dimple & Divot x Gumtree Golf & Nature Club – Species Brush American sycamore
body_html:
These Gumtree Golf & Nature x Dimple & Divot premium golf brushes are made in the US and carved from three different species of American trees. All brushes feature a nickel trigger snap and tonal paracord to match the natural wood tones. 

The American sycamore (Platanus occidentalis) is found along riverbanks and old fairways across the eastern states, it wears its history on its bar, peeling layers of gray, cream, and green over its long life. In summer, its broad leaves cast some must needed shade on the course and in winter, its pale trunk gleams against the rest of the woods, impossible to miss. It’s signature grain is evident in this golf brush.

title: Dimple & Divot x Gumtree Golf & Nature Club – Species Brush
body_html:
These Gumtree Golf & Nature x Dimple & Divot premium golf brushes are made in the US and carved from three different species of American trees. All brushes feature a nickel trigger snap and tonal paracord to match the natural wood tones. 

The sugar maple (Acer saccharum) stands as one of nature’s quiet masterpieces. Native to the forests of eastern North America, it’s best known for two gifts, the slow drip of its sap each spring, and the unmatched blaze of color it brings each autumn. Its wood, dense and fine-grained, has long been shaped into instruments, clubs, tables and now this golf brush, things meant to last.

title: Ciel Glue 'Land Ahoy'
body_html:
Adventure meets precision in "Land Ahoy", a whimsical collage where the world of golf is seen through an entirely new lens — literally. This limited edition print features a dramatic view of a distant golf course as seen through a monocular or telescope, evoking the thrill of discovery and the long game ahead.

Crafted from vintage golf magazines, the artwork is rich in nostalgic detail and layered meaning. The scene blends the structured calm of the golf world with the poetic vastness of exploration, turning the act of "spotting the green" into a metaphor for pursuit, patience, and perspective. It’s a playful visual pun that speaks to both dreamers and die-hard golfers.

Limited Edition of 50: Hand-numbered and part of an exclusive series.

Material: Printed on luxurious 300 g fine art paper, offering crisp detail and museum-quality depth.

Size 30 X 40cm

Handmade Collage: Composed using original vintage golf imagery, ensuring each piece radiates authenticity and charm.

Made in Portugal: Conceptualized and designed amidst the rolling hills and coastal beauty of Portugal.

Whether you see it as a journey, a target, or a whimsical escape, "Land Ahoy" brings a bold yet serene energy to any wall — ideal for golf lovers, art collectors, and anyone who appreciates a clever twist on a classic theme.

(Frame not included)

title: Ciel Glue 'Fairway'
body_html:
"Fairway" is a visual journey through the soul of the golf course — a collage that reveals the landscape in layers, much like the game itself. This artwork peels back the course piece by piece, from tee to green, showcasing rolling hills, bunkers, fairways, and roughs in a stacked, almost geological composition. Each layer is a memory, a challenge, a step toward the hole.

Crafted from original vintage golf magazines, "Fairway" is both a tribute to course design and a quiet metaphor for progression — how each shot, like each layer, brings us closer to the goal. The result is part map, part dream, and wholly grounded in the textures and tones of classic golf.

Material: Printed on premium 250g fine art paper for deep color and long-lasting quality.

Handmade Collage: Built from vintage golf imagery, each detail rich with mid-century charm and texture.

Made in Portugal: Inspired by Portugal’s undulating greens and sculpted landscapes.

Whether you’re a player, a lover of design, or simply someone who finds beauty in rhythm and repetition, "Fairway" brings structure, depth, and serenity to your walls — a quiet homage to the layered poetry of the game.

(Frame not included)

title: Ciel Glue 'Hook'
body_html:
In "Hook", elegance meets revelation. This imaginative collage captures the precise moment a lady golfer strikes the ball — and with that single swing, she tears open the surface, revealing the world of golf hidden beneath. It’s a striking metaphor for breakthrough, precision, and the hidden beauty unlocked through movement.

Composed from vintage golf magazine clippings, "Hook" plays with the tension between control and unpredictability. The female figure, composed and poised, becomes a force of discovery — exposing layers of texture, landscape, and meaning with one decisive hit.

Material: Printed on premium 250 g fine art paper for lasting color and detail.

Handmade Collage: Built from original vintage materials, offering authenticity and nostalgic charm.

Made in Portugal: Conceived and created in a land where golf courses meet cliffs, light, and history.

Whether you're drawn to its surreal twist, bold composition, or vintage energy, "Hook" is a compelling addition to any art collection — a moment of action frozen in time, revealing more than just the game.

(Frame not included)

title: Ciel Glue 'Nuked'
body_html:
"Nuked" captures the obsessive energy behind the pursuit of the perfect shot. In this surreal and captivating collage, a lone golfer channels every ounce of focus, power, and precision into a single swing — so explosive in intent, it sends shockwaves through the landscape. A towering mushroom cloud rises in the distance, not as destruction, but as a metaphor: the inner detonation of ambition, pressure, and pure impact.

Hand-assembled from vintage golf magazine clippings, "Nuked" is rich in texture, irony, and quiet drama. It speaks to the intense internal moment every golfer knows — when the world narrows to one shot, one movement, one chance to get it absolutely right.

Material: Printed on 250 g fine art paper for museum-quality depth and lasting brilliance.

Handmade Collage: Composed using authentic vintage imagery, giving each detail character and nostalgic soul.

Made in Portugal: Conceived among Portugal’s fairways, where beauty meets intensity.

“Nuked” is a bold meditation on perfectionism, pressure, and the quiet violence of precision. Ideal for those who see the game not just as a sport, but as a metaphor for mastery.

(Frame not included)

title: Ciel Glue 'Moliets'
body_html:
"Moliets" is where the golf course meets the coast, and the rhythm of golf merges with the pulse of the Atlantic. Inspired by the sweeping pines, golden dunes, and world-class waves of Les Landes, this collage captures the harmony of surf and turf in one timeless frame. A lone golfer takes a swing not far from breaking waves — a serene dialogue between sport, nature, and freedom.

Assembled from vintage golf magazine clippings, "Moliets" blends retro charm with coastal calm. The layered textures echo the region’s wild-yet-orderly beauty: neatly kept fairways bordered by sand, forest, and sea spray. It’s a quiet tribute to a place where the game slows down, and nature speaks louder than the scorecard.

Material: Printed on 250 g fine art paper, ensuring crisp detail and a rich, archival finish.

Handmade Collage: Built with original vintage imagery, offering depth, nostalgia, and character.

Made in Portugal: Designed with a coastal perspective, connecting two shorelines through one vision.

“Moliets” is perfect for those who find peace in the balance — between land and ocean, action and stillness, the front nine and the sea breeze. A portrait of place, play, and the slow art of escape.

(Frame not included)

title: The Links Diary No.12
body_html: In The Links Diary No.12, Richard Pennell discovers the joys of Rosapenna. Boris Lietzow shows us round his hickory shop in Gullane, and Jamie Darling plays Among Lofty Sandhills experiencing the original 12 holes of Prestwick. Seaton Carew prospers against all odds, and Tommy Twigley's 56 degree wedge, affectionately know as Uncle Phil, goes missing. The true face of golf is not Scottie Scheffler or Rory McIlroy, or some other factory-produced, absurdly wealthy, golf professional. It is 86 year old Sandy Watson of Southend, who lives 50 yards from the 1st tee at Dunaverty. All of this and more in The Links Diary No.12.

title: Depeche Golf Issue 1
body_html:
Step into a world of new, fresh perspectives on the game of golf. Our first issue offers a curated collection of captivating stories, stunning visuals, and thought-provoking essays.

Find in-depth portraits of golf’s most colourful characters, explorations from the world’s most iconic and most obscure courses, and shed light on untold chapters of the game’s history.

Tied together by state-of-the-art design, Issue #1 is printed on heavy, natural paper and appeals to all senses. It’s a read that will do what a good round of golf does for you: calm your mind, lift your spirit, and expand your horizon.

title: The Links Diary No.11
body_html: In No.11 Jim Hartsell discovers the joys of a small community club set amongst the rolling hills of the Trossachs in 'Not All Those Who Wander Are Lost'. We find 'What Lies Beneath' Brian Barnes' personality, quirky dress sense and that beer can. 'Coat and Tie Required' in a match played annually between Muirfield and Iona that brings an unlikely bunch together in friendship and golf. There are 52 caddies at Gullane, only 51 of them are men. Abercrombie Nisbet describes what it's like to be the only female caddie at Gullane... so far. All of this and more in The Links Diary No.11.

title: The Links Diary No.5
body_html: In No.5 we explore one man's obsession with golf memorabilia that fills his entire spare room. A visit to Askernish where Jim Harstell's expectations far exceed what he could have ever imagined. Murray Bothwell caught up with Mr Carnoustie - Trevor Williamson, as he tells of his love affair with the famous links. All of this and more in the latest edition of The Links Diary.

title: The Links Diary No.6
body_html: In No.6 we venture North to the Links of Brora as Jim Hartsell answers the question why do we love golf? We've all had that moment when we believe we can play this game. That lightbulb moment when everything aligns, when it all seems to flow so effortlessly. That was not the case for a crane operator, in the north of England, in the 1970's as he aimed to become the champion golfer of the year in The Ballad of Count Manfred von Hoffmanstel. Ollie Allison asked himself, Is 12 the perfect number? as he explored a wonderous golf course on an island off the west coast of Scotland. Tempers flare on a round with a golf clubs most notorious aggravated member as Reece Witters delivers another highly amusing short story in The Whistly Nostril. All of this and more in No.6

title: The Links Diary No.7
body_html: In No.7 we take a deep dive into the Road Hole of the Old Course at St Andrews with Clayton, Devries and Pont architect Sam Cooper as he gives his low down on why it's such a brilliant design. Small is Beautiful as Dan Davies fulfilled his lifelong dream of building his own golf course, in a orchard, in his back garden. We caught up with a group of American golfers for a Guinness filled night of laughter at The Jigger Inn, and Murray Bothwell pens a unique folklore tale from the links of Royal Dornoch staged in the middle of the night. Golfers and their lawns, for some it's an obsession for perfection. Reece Witters gives his amusing and clever take on Harold Whifflesworth pursuit of the perfect surface. What was it like teeing it up with Tom Watson in the 2009 Open Championship final round? Jim Hartsell speaks with Matt Goggin as he gives his perspective of that Sunday round. All of this and more in TLD No.7.

title: The Links Diary No.8
body_html: In No.8 we take a walk in the park in the city centre of Edinburgh for some short hole golf with the members of Brunstfield Short Hole Golf Club. Content is King and clicks are currency as Gary Henderson explores the rabbit hole of social media golf. Packing for the North of Scotland in late November is a precarious business. Author Richard Pennell chases the light before winter sets in, in The Alchemy of Adventure. Jim Hartsell pens another love letter to golf as he reminisces playing in the Iona Open in one of Scotland's most remote golf courses. Straight out of a fairytale sums up the day Ladybank Golf Club had in the summer of 1983 when Jack and Seve turned up. All of this and more in 144 pages of golf for the soul.

title: The Links Diary No.9
body_html: In No.9 We discover a story of a Millionaire management consultant who started a scheme to train selected young professional golfers in a bid to produce a major champion by 1967. Jim Hartsell pens a love letter to a 9 holer in an enchanted glen on the Isle of Arran. Arnold Palmer steered the way for the American onslaught of the Open Championship in his usual flamboyant manner, and Gary Henderson admits to shamefully only discovering the joys of North Berwick in recent years. Gift yourself some quiet time with 144 pages of golf for the soul. All of this and more in TLD No.9.

title: The Links Diary No.10
body_html: In No.10 travel disruptions strike fear in to a father and son as they cling on to the hope of making their Old Course tee time. Murray Bothwell pens a letter to golf and asks the question of why we play the game. A trip to Machrihanish and the unknown as Sam Lowes Raby throws caution to the wind to tee it up with a bunch of strangers in Golf, Guinness and the Ghost of Old Tom. A weakness for charity shops and what you might find hidden among the tat has Richard Pennell searching for forgotten clubs in Dearly Preloved. Stewart Fotheringham has been the greenkeeper at Shiskine on the Isle of Arran since the day he left school. He's never known another job. "I'm an artist and Shiskine is my Canvas." All of this and more in The Links Diary No.10
